It further explains that 'As the distance between the viewer's eye and the viewing plane increases, the angle of divergence between rays decreases,' and that as distance approaches infinity, divergence approaches zero. Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

The pinhole camera model, which simulates depth by positioning the eye behind the image plane at a distance $f$ (focal length), is the standard geometric foundation for ray generation in computer graphics [S1, S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the pinhole camera model simulates depth by positioning the eye behind the image plane at a distance $f$ (focal length) and is the standard geometric foundation for ray generation. Source [S1] explicitly supports this by stating: 'To do this, we can simulate a pinhole camera by positioning the eye behind the image plane... The distance between the eye and the image plane is analogue to the focal length...'. It further details the ray generation process (calculating direction as the difference between image plane point and eye). Source [S3] provides implementation details for a pinhole camera model that generates ray origins and directions based on camera pose and field of view, consistent with the geometric foundation described. Both sources confirm the specific mechanism (eye position, distance $f$, ray generation) described in the claim.
